newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian competition watchdog slaps ad agencies.
newsitem.headline: Italian competition watchdog slaps ad agencies.

text.p: Italy's anti-trust watchdog has given advertising agency associations 60 days to come up with new guidelines on prices and bids for new business after judging that the current practice is anti-competitive.

The body, which has been investigating the industry for six months, said in a statement that price lists drawn up by advertising agencies for non-commissionable work, such as designing brochures or logos, amounted to "unlawful agreements".
It also decided that standard practices regarding invitations to pitch for new business -- which in some cases limit the number of agencies able to take part -- were restrictive.
The anti-trust body did not, however, impose any sanctions.

Fidelio Perchinelli, director of industry association AssAP which represents 56 large advertising agencies, denied there was a cartel arrangement in the industry and said the practices had been standard in the industry for more than 30 years.
"We will now have to renew them in the light of the new reality," he told Reuters.

A senior advertising agency executive, however, dismissed the anti-trust body's concerns. He said restrictive practices did not exist since the price lists were never binding and it would remain up to companies to decide how to invite new business.
"Not much will change. You can't make a big private company invite 100 agencies to pitch. It would be chaos," he said.

Italy's advertising industry, including direct marketing, promotions, public relations and sponsorship, had billings (total spend) of 21.5 trillion lire ($14 billion) in 1996 against some 20 trillion in 1995, according to industry body UPA. ($1=1,538 lire)
